discovery: Fluctuation theorems and nonequilibrium work relations, founding stochastic thermodynamics

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

motivation: For over a century the second law was a statement about averages near equilibrium. Evans and co-workers' fluctuation theorem (1993-94) and Jarzynski's equality (1997) showed that exact identities hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium, relating the fluctuations of entropy production and work to equilibrium free energies. Seifert then built a consistent framework of stochastic thermodynamics, defining entropy along single trajectories and generalizing these relations. Together these results turned the second law into an exact statement for small systems and created a new field. They have been verified quantitatively in single-molecule pulling, colloidal, electronic and trapped-ion experiments. They are used to extract free energies of biomolecules, and they underpin the modern thermodynamics of information, from Maxwell's demon and Landauer erasure to feedback control and quantum thermodynamics. This is a rare case where clean, general theory opened an entire experimental and conceptual domain.
